Information since the September meeting points to a still-strong labor market and moderate growth, but weakness in business fixed investment and exports alongside below-2% inflation and low market-based inflation compensation gives the statement a cautious, dovish tilt. This aligns with evidence that downturns in investment materially weigh on real GDP (investment spending often accounting for output declines) and with findings that monetary policy affects real activity in the short run (Sims; McCallum and Nelson; B. Friedman). With inflation expectations stable yet below target, easing is consistent with flexible inflation-targeting guidance and Phillips curve evidence emphasizing the role of expectations in inflation dynamics (Svensson; Rudebusch; Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido). Overall, tone is positive on current conditions but risk-aware on the outlook.
